content.title: Recap: Best moments, news from 5-game Sunday
content.text: Nikola Jokić tallies his NBA-leading 28th triple-double with 22 points, 14 rebounds and 14 assists during Denver’s 128-112 win over Portland. (Photo by Garrett Ellwood/NBAE via Getty Images) Check out the best of Sunday’s 5-game slate with the NBA.com live blog, featuring all of the meaningful moments, performances, observations, news, notes and highlights. 2026 Playoff Picture: Where teams stand Last night’s live blog: LeBron, KD make history to highlight wild Saturday Download the NBA App What we know after Sunday’s games: Nikola Jokić (22 pts, 14 reb, 14 ast) notched his 192nd career triple-double (2nd in NBA history) in Denver’s win against Portland. It was his 85th triple-double through three quarters, good for the most since 1997-98 (play-by-play era). The Knicks scored 32+ points in every quarter of their 145-113 win over Washington to win their sixth consecutive game. Karl-Anthony Towns (26 pts, 16 reb) recorded his league-leading 50th double-double. Minnesota picked up a gritty 10-point win over the Celtics for the first time in Boston in 7,685 days (March 6, 2005) behind Bones Hyland (23 pts, 3 3PM) and Jaden McDaniels (19 pts, 6 reb, 3 ast). Devin Booker (25 pts, 6 ast) and Jalen Green (20 pts, 7 ast) combined for 45 points on 17-for-30 shooting (56.7%) to snap a five-game losing streak for the Suns. Conference contenders collide when the Timberwolves visit the Celtics on Sunday Night Basketball. Deni Avdija and the Portland Trail Blazers visit Nikola Jokić and the Denver Nuggets for the first of two primetime matchups on this light Sunday of pro hoops (5 ET, NBA TV). Portland (9th in West) will attempt to win a fourth consecutive game and continue their late season push to secure a spot in the SoFi Play-In Tournament, while Denver (5th in West) tries to make up ground in a packed race for top six. In the national spotlight, Julius Randle and the Timberwolves take on Jaylen Brown and the Celtics on Sunday Night Basketball (8 ET, NBC/Peacock). Minnesota looks to right the ship without Anthony Edwards (knee), and Boston takes aim at a fifth consecutive victory. Here’s tonight’s complete schedule: Portland Trail Blazers vs Denver Nuggets (5 ET, NBA TV) Brooklyn Nets vs Sacramento Kings (6 ET) Washington Wizards vs New York Knicks (7:30 ET) Minnesota Timberwolves vs Boston Celtics (8 ET, NBC/Peacock) Toronto Raptors vs Phoenix Suns (9 ET)
